chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, raising it, said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not teach your women Surah Yusuf, nor recite it to them, for therein is the strife, and teach them Surah Al-Nur, for therein is the advice.'
ai.seo_question: Why should women not be taught Surah Yusuf according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the narrative potency of Surah Yusuf, which contains elements of 'fitnah' (temptation or strife) that may require guidance, and the didactic clarity of Surah Al-Nur, which offers direct moral instruction. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of contextual pedagogy, where the emotional and narrative depth of Joseph's story is weighed against the legal and ethical clarity of the Light chapter for domestic education.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said,

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not teach your womenfolk Surah Yusuf (Chapter 12) nor recite it to them, for therein is the strife, and teach them Surah Al Noor (Chapter 24), for therein is the advice’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya’qub ibn Salim in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “‘

Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not teach your women chapter twelve of the Quran and do not read it for them; in it there is sedition, instead teach them Chapter twenty-four of the Quran because in it there are exhortations.’”
